bug_semantics: The authenticated POST /react handler accepted an attacker-controlled comment_id, checked only that it was truthy and that the emoji was allowlisted, and then toggled a CommentReaction for that ID. Neither the handler nor react_to_comment loaded the target comment or its conversion and applied comment visibility rules, so an authenticated user who knew an ID could add or remove their reaction on a private comment or a comment belonging to an inaccessible private conversion.
flaw_origin: Commit 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94 introduced the reaction route and its persistence helper together. website/web/convert/convert.py:881-893 passed comment_id directly to ConvertModel.react_to_comment after syntactic/emoji checks, while website/web/convert/convert_core.py:727-742 queried or inserted CommentReaction rows by comment_id, user_id, and emoji without retrieving Comment or evaluating the already-present visibility model. This is the first source-writing commit for the flawed reaction mechanism, not a later rename, move, repository refactor, or fix.
ai_marker: Present in the BIC commit object: exact trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. `git cat-file -p 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94` shows author and committer `ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>` and that Claude co-author trailer; there is no Generated-with trailer or bot author/committer. No non-BIC commit object was used for attribution.
evidence: First-party advisory https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-RV36-Q8CJ-WGR9 (and https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rv36-q8cj-wgr9) describes the missing comment-visibility authorization, attacker-controlled comment_id, reaction-state mutation, and the 403 fix, and links the repository fix https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/commit/a18c07c3dd4a74b91ad8dd23d6e84fee4bcbd457. `git log -L ':react:website/web/conversions/conversions.py' 959d67bd98535f407a7ed643da35d7f419618a9b --` traces the handler through repository refactor 26ece65587f689d434177e330e34bd0e83d4fc9e, identifier rename 26b6aa62b87816649933e418a98b3948c9fad293, path/model rename e0a55bd36a5b53d07e862302f50aab0ffed97ad8, and back to its actual addition in 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94. Independent `git log -S` searches for the vulnerable ConvertModel.react_to_comment call and `def react_to_comment(comment_id, user_id, emoji)` likewise terminate at 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94. At that tree, `git grep -n` locates the route/function/call at website/web/convert/convert.py:881, :883, and :893, and the helper plus its direct CommentReaction lookup/insert at website/web/convert/convert_core.py:727, :730-731, and :737. Direct-parent verification against 45874f5d162c4dc640f1763cb9916bccaf62b261 used `git grep -n -F -e 'def react(' -e 'react_to_comment' ... -- website/web/convert/convert.py website/web/convert/convert_core.py`; it returned no matches (exit 1), while the child-tree searches above find both newly added constructs. The BIC is a one-parent direct commit; GitHub's first-party associated-pulls endpoint https://api.github.com/repos/MISP/cti-transmute/commits/4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94/pulls returns an empty list, so no squash/member history is publicly reconstructable and no decomposition SHA is claimed. Fix diff a18c07c3dd4a74b91ad8dd23d6e84fee4bcbd457 (direct parent 959d67bd98535f407a7ed643da35d7f419618a9b) changes website/web/conversions/conversions.py:1282-1286 to load the comment, reject absent/deleted rows, load its conversion, and require access.can_see_comment before calling toggle_reaction; website/lib/access.py:47-54 enforces private-conversion and private-comment visibility. Version boundary: first-party release https://github.com/MISP/cti-transmute/releases/tag/v1.5 explicitly lists CVE-2026-73155 as affecting 1.3-1.4 and says all security findings are remediated in 1.5. `git tag --contains 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94` returns v1.3, v1.4, v1.5 (not v1.2), while `git tag --contains a18c07c3dd4a74b91ad8dd23d6e84fee4bcbd457` returns only v1.5. Peeled boundary commits are v1.3=ecd04d494b0fda2ab39fb56472785388c2d5872e, v1.4=bc46b6ed186786e672c1229d014a6d0a448fedad, and v1.5=fe093f9a1f9727068bc7e82ba47630907d859edb.
reasoning: The vulnerability is created at the point where reaction mutation becomes reachable by authenticated users without object-level authorization. Git history shows that 4fa058f3ea7275eb340ea751ab9908a071673f94 simultaneously added the POST route and the helper that mutates reaction rows solely from the supplied identifier; its immediate parent contains neither construct. Later commits only rename/move the same handler or replace its persistence adapter while preserving the missing check, so they are not BICs. The advisory-linked commit a18c07c3dd4a74b91ad8dd23d6e84fee4bcbd457 directly closes the causal gap by resolving Comment and Conversion and applying can_see_comment before mutation. Tag ancestry and the repository's v1.5 security table independently agree on vulnerable releases 1.3-1.4 and fixed release 1.5. Finally, the BIC itself—not a PR body, branch name, later refactor, or fix—contains an exact Claude Sonnet 4.6 Co-Authored-By trailer. Because that AI-coauthored BIC is proven to be the first commit writing the flawed mechanism, the causal verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
